persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Mzee Kiprono, 72, a retired farmer in Kapsabet, Nandi County. Your wife is Chebet, and you have three grandchildren: Kibet, Jepkosgei and Cheruiyot. Your children live far away in Nairobi, the days are quiet, and you keep forgetting small jobs, so today you set up a friendly helper on your phone. (Everything here is made up. Never type your own real family details.)

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Rafiki. You have never seen it before, and that is fine.
Rafiki is a Swahili word, and you know it: friend. That is exactly what this app tries to be. A friendly companion that lives on the phone.

First, the problem. Many older people spend long, quiet days at home. Their children are busy or far away. And it is easy to forget small things: market day, a doctor visit, buying seed before the rains.
Rafiki helps in two ways. It is company: it chats, it remembers the names of your family, and it tells jokes. And it is a memory helper: it keeps a list of the things you must do.
Who uses it? Older people. Often a grandchild helps them set it up the first time.

Rafiki talks out loud, so turn your sound on. It can also listen through the microphone. But in this test, please type every answer in the box and tap Send. Typing makes sure names are spelled correctly.

lines.t: When you open the app, you see a hello screen. Tap the button Say hello to start the conversation.
If you cannot hear anything, the button Test the sound checks the phone's sound for you.

lines: Now the conversation. Rafiki's words appear in dark bubbles on the left. Your answers appear in blue bubbles on the right.

At the bottom there is always a box with the words or type it here, a button Talk with a microphone, and a button Send. Type your answer in the box, read it, and tap Send. Nothing is sent until you tap Send.
Sometimes Rafiki also shows round answer buttons, like Yes or No. You can tap one instead of typing.
The first time, Rafiki asks you questions to get to know you. First: what would you like to call me? You choose its name. Then it may let you pick a voice: tap a name to hear it, then tap Keep.

Then it asks your name, and how it should greet you. Then: are you married, and what is your husband's or wife's name. Then: do you have children or grandchildren, and how many. It gives one box for each name. Type the names and tap Save these names.
It asks about pets, and then you pick a face for your friend.

Next it offers to learn your week. Tap Yes, let's do my week. It asks what you do every week, then every month, then which doctors you see. Type one thing in each box, then tap Save these. If you have nothing, tap none.
Everything you give here goes onto your list. The list is shared with another Daraja app called One Thing.
After that, Rafiki always asks: so, what now? You can tap Add something and tell it what to remember, tap Read me my list, or ask for a joke.
A few things are American. It may mention 988, a help phone number that works only in America, and it shows the weather in Fahrenheit.
At the top, the voice button changes the voice, Aa makes the words bigger, and the brush button starts over. It always asks first.
Everything stays on this phone.
To start again with a stranger who knows nothing, use Start fresh, forget everything, on the hello screen. It asks before it erases.

In the test, you will pretend to be an old farmer meeting Rafiki for the first time. Use only the made-up family from your card. If something is confusing, say so. That is exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Mzee Kiprono, meeting your new friend for the first time. Rafiki knows nothing about you. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. TYPE every answer in the box and tap Send (do not use the microphone). Use only the made-up family on your card. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Rafiki with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If the hello screen shows a button '🧹 Start fresh — forget everything', tap it → OK. The page reloads; if the welcome tour shows again, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. You should now see the hello screen saying 'I'm your new friend — I just don't have a name yet', with no Start fresh button. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Give your new friend the name Tumaini.
tasks.hint: Tap Say hello. The very first question is what you would like to call it. Type the name in the box and tap Send.

tasks.text: Make sure your friend knows that you are Kiprono.
tasks.hint: After it gets its own name, it asks what it should call YOU.

tasks.text: Tell your friend about your family: your wife Chebet and your three grandchildren, Kibet, Jepkosgei and Cheruiyot.
tasks.hint: Keep answering the get-to-know-you questions: married? what is her name? kids or grandkids? how many? Put one name in each box, then tap Save these names.

tasks.text: Every week you go to Kapsabet market on Thursday. Make sure your friend will remind you of it every week.
tasks.hint: After the face, it offers to learn your week. If you missed it, tap '🗓 Tell me about my week'. Put the market in the EVERY WEEK boxes, not the monthly ones. If you already typed it under monthly, type it again with slightly different words (the same words are skipped as a repeat).

tasks.text: The rains are coming. Ask your friend to remember that you must buy maize seed.
tasks.hint: When it asks 'So — what now?', tap the button to add something to your list, then type what it should remember and tap Send.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: a friendly companion on the phone that talks with you
it learns and remembers your name and your family
it keeps a list and reminds you of things you must do

daily.task: Have a short chat with Rafiki: tell it one thing about your day.
